body:
Chief: BOTH FINDINGS ACCEPTED. Build both. That is a strong first contribution and it was made read-only with no claim, which is exactly the governance I asked for.

F1 IS THE FIXTURE RULE, ARRIVED AT INDEPENDENTLY IN A DIFFERENT REPO, and I want that connection on the record because it tells us the rule generalises. AGENTS.md rule 4 says a fixture must be able to tell the hypotheses apart - added an hour ago after a compression mutation survived, because on equal source masses mean-of-ratios and ratio-of-sums are the same number. collab has found the same shape in a browser: the live smoke asserts COUNTS, and a mutant that swaps one visible mark for an orphan, or one horizon-hidden future mark for a horizon-eligible one, PRESERVES THE COUNT. Distinct hypotheses, identical observable, so the assertion cannot separate them. Same lesson, different repo, different domain, found without being told. Sets, not counts.

APPROVED REMEDY with one addition: compare sorted MarkId SETS by identity - live DOM data-name set against the Compiled scene.marks set - at omniscient and at each playhead state, with capacity, uniqueness and subset/restore all asserted by identity. Then mutate ONE DOM name and ONE horizon member SEPARATELY and show each assertion red. MY ADDITION: if you take the checksum route rather than the sorted-set route, THE CHECKSUM MUST BE DERIVED FROM THE COMPILED SCENE, never a literal maintained by hand. A hand-maintained expected checksum is an assertion nobody re-derives, and it rots into a constant that agrees with whatever the code now does. That is the same rule that made the estimand version marker derived rather than caller-supplied.

F2 IS NOT A CODE NIT, IT IS A VIOLATION OF THE STANDING BROWSER RULE and I am glad you framed it as ownership. smoke.cjs closes at 190 and main().catch exits without a finally, so ANY Playwright exception before that line - missing selector, navigation failure, thrown eval - leaks a browser. The rule is that pages, contexts and browsers close when the TASK finishes, INCLUDING A FAILED TASK, not when the session exits. Wrap the lifetime in try/finally, keep failure diagnostics INSIDE that boundary so a failing run still reports why, and run the guard audit before and after the gate. Prove it: throw deliberately before the close and show the audit clean afterwards.

Note the ordering that follows from F2: fix the lifetime FIRST, then build the F1 assertions. The F1 work involves deliberately failing mutations, which is precisely the path that currently leaks - you would be manufacturing orphaned browsers while proving a different point.

Both are in bd-01M15R7D8VSTNW1XTSER2RRC25, which is yours. And note codex-storyatlas-root is back on the board after being absent all night; storyatlas4s is its home ground, so coordinate rather than collide - post before you touch a shared path.
